prize_parts.citation: For turning ubiquitin-proteasome chemistry into a design principle: small molecules that bring a chosen protein to an E3 ligase and so cause its degradation, whether built as bifunctional PROTACs or discovered as cereblon-directed molecular glues

statement.case_for: After the first round my preferred configuration is unchanged: B067 alone, credited to Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The scientific case is that regulated proteolysis has become a defined chemical reaction that can be designed. A small molecule brings an E3 ligase and a target together, the target is ubiquitinated and destroyed, and the effect has been reproduced by many independent groups on many targets. That is a mechanism understood at the level of a chemical event, and it gives biologists a general tool, which is what I look for. The round-1 exchange showed that all members who discuss B067 agree on the principle and on Crews and Deshaies; the dispute is only the third name and the reach of the citation. I choose Handa because cereblon identification is a measured molecular explanation of why thalidomide-type drugs act. It gave the field its second workable E3 handle and links the PROTAC and glue branches into one achievement, so the citation can be defended in both branches without claiming more than these three people support.
statement.case_against: The reservations are real. No heterobifunctional degrader is broadly approved, most of the field depends on two ligases (CRBN and VHL), and I would want evidence that degradation is robust beyond favourable targets. Attribution is the most contested on the shortlist: any three names leave out Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim, and a single citation spanning PROTACs and glues risks reading as a merger of two discoveries with different origins. My choice of Handa over Ciulli is a judgment call that four colleagues made the other way, and I cannot show it is better; I only think it matches the citation as I have written it. A committee that wants a PROTAC-only citation would reasonably choose Ciulli, and I would not treat that as an error.

responses.point: Aili credits Ciulli for the structure-guided VHL ligand that made PROTACs drug-like, questions how much of degrader chemistry is new beyond linker and ligand optimisation, and flags the glue branch as a strong competing claim.
responses.response: I accept that Ciulli's VHL ligand and ternary-complex structures turned a peptide-based proof of principle into drug-like chemistry, and that is a measured result. But I read the optimisation worry the other way round. Cereblon identification showed that a class of drugs already in patients worked through this mechanism, so the principle was validated before PROTACs existed, and that is why I keep Handa. If the committee writes the citation around bifunctional molecules only, Ciulli is the better third name and I would support that configuration over none. I have not moved, because the glue branch has the longer clinical record.

responses.point: Aqvist says the Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli trio is a coherent story with a clear citation, but concedes it is weaker if the committee judges that glues and PROTACs are one achievement.
responses.response: This is the conditional I find decisive. Aqvist's own test, that the trio is weaker if the strands are one achievement, is met by the mechanism: both end in an E3 ligase bringing a target to ubiquitination, and the cereblon result explains the older drugs in exactly those terms. I do not claim Ciulli's contribution is smaller; the quantitative work on cooperativity that Aqvist values is real. My claim is only that a trio without a glue name must restrict the citation to PROTACs, which then looks narrower than the field. I will not count agreement among four members on Ciulli as evidence about attribution.

responses.point: Linke, whose earlier first-place candidate was B049, now prefers B067 for a simple general principle that gives a new capability, and acknowledges that this favours drug-modality impact over principle.
responses.response: I think his reasoning about capability is right, and I agree that phase separation is a real physical idea. My reservation about B049 is a measurement one: the founding observation of liquid-like P granules is solid, but much of the cellular evidence uses overexpression or non-physiological concentrations, and I have seen similar assumptions fail when quantities were measured carefully. A narrow citation limited to liquid-like demixing as an organising mechanism would answer the artefact point for me, but the physiological role still needs confirmation at endogenous levels. For this year B067 has the better replication record, so I keep B049 as a later candidate and do not put it ahead.

responses.point: Somfai keeps C-N coupling (B013) first for maturity, wide routine use and a clean two-person credit, with Kosugi as a precedence footnote.
responses.response: I agree that B013 is the best-verified and cleanest attribution on the shortlist and I would not oppose it. It does not change my preference, because the 2010 prize recognised Pd-catalysed cross-coupling as a concept and C-N coupling extends it to another bond. A clean credit strengthens his case but cannot be the deciding criterion by itself, since it describes how the field developed and not how much it changed what chemists can do. Degraders offer something chemists could not do before, removing a protein by design, and I rank that above a mature refinement.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers B069 (Gray, Winkler) plus B052 (Liu) as a two-part prize on chemical principles in natural and engineered systems, with B067 as first alternative and a note that B067 may be stronger if attribution can be settled.
responses.response: His note that B067 may be the stronger choice if attribution can be settled is the point I try to address: my configuration settles it by naming Handa for the glue branch beside Crews and Deshaies, which I think is defensible. I would not support the two-part B069 plus B052 prize for myself. Base editing is an alternative of mine but sits close to CRISPR 2020 with long-term outcomes unknown, and electron tunnelling in proteins is largely textbook and overlaps with 1992. He has not yet said what result would show that the Gray and Winkler tunnelling-pathway interpretation changes current research, and that remains the question that decides maturity for me.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat PROTACs and glues as a single achievement; if it does not, I have no strong view on which strand should be dropped, and a two-part prize must still stay within three names.
Handa versus Ciulli as third name is a judgment call, and I could be persuaded to Ciulli if the citation is limited to bifunctional molecules.
Whether the lack of an approved heterobifunctional degrader makes 2026 early; I have not verified current clinical status beyond what colleagues reported.
Whether dependence on only CRBN and VHL is a real limit on generality or a feature of an early field.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited B067 person: I know none of Crews, Deshaies, Handa or Ciulli as collaborators. I use protein-depletion tools in genome-maintenance work, which makes me a user of the method but not a party to it. As in round 1, I note a mild interest in base editing and sequencing as nucleic-acid tools; this does not affect my choice and I do not think it requires recusal.
